# Fixture Guideline on Glove Use (Revised)

## Background

Health workers must clean their hands before and after patient contact. The revision replaces the earlier fixture guideline. Glove use is a supplement to hand hygiene and never a substitute for it. Contaminated gloves spread organisms between patients and surfaces. Gloves must be changed between patients and between dirty and clean body sites on the same patient. Hand hygiene is required after glove removal because gloves may have invisible defects. Alcohol-based handrub is the preferred method unless hands are visibly soiled. Soap and water must be used when hands are visibly dirty or after caring for patients with infectious diarrhoea. Staff must keep nails short and must not wear artificial nails in clinical areas. Rings and wrist watches must be removed before performing hand hygiene. Skin care products should be used to prevent irritant dermatitis. Facilities must place handrub dispensers at the point of care. Compliance must be monitored through direct observation every quarter. Results must be fed back to ward teams within two weeks. Training must be repeated every year for all clinical staff. New staff must complete training before their first clinical shift. Observers must be trained and validated before auditing. Audit tools must record opportunities and actions separately. Low compliance must trigger an improvement plan within one month.

### Monitoring Details

Observation sessions last twenty minutes. Each session records at least ten opportunities.
